title: Support Bikram Sambat month intervals for Targets and UHC
notes: DRAFT: built from a manual review of the PR, not yet from benchmark runs; severities are estimates, and `rejected` items are wrong findings anticipated from that review, not ones runs have made. Closed without merging: its only comment is a maintainer saying the underlying issue belongs to the DMP 2026 program and isn't ready to be worked on, which gives no findings away; there are no reviews or inline comments. The PR has no closing issue (it lists #10652, #10707 and #6797 as 'Related issues', and its title has no `(#N)`), so the completeness review sees no linked issue and the PR description is the sole statement of intent. #10652 holds the design discussion behind it: the instance-wide `uhc.visit_count.use_bikram_sambat_months` flag, and keeping target docs stored under the Gregorian YYYY-MM of the interval end, which stays unique because a BS month never starts and ends in the same Gregorian month. #11237 later implemented the same config key and was merged; it is a useful reference but chose BS-tagged target docs, so its extra changes (DHIS export, provider-wireup tags) are not defects of this PR. Its defects are in the interval maths, the previous-period tag, an unconverted UHC caller and existing specs it breaks.

code-review.notes: `severity` is an estimate of the severity the finding deserves, from a manual review; it is to be checked against OCR's own ratings once runs exist (the most common across the runs that reported it, the higher one on a tie; a comment that covers several items gives its severity only to the item that is its main point). `extra_credit` holds correct findings a review earns credit for but isn't marked down for missing.

required.summary: getBikramSambatInterval and the BS branch of getPreviousInterval pass a Date object to bikramSambat.toBik, which runs Date.parse(String(date)) and counts whole days from the library's epoch, 1913-04-12T12:30Z. The library expects a 'YYYY-MM-DD' string (parsed as UTC midnight); with a Date carrying a time, any moment after 12:30 UTC (18:15 in Nepal) is read as the next BS day. So every evening in Nepal from 18:15, and on the last day of a BS month (or the day before month_start_date) getCurrent returns the next interval, which hasn't started and doesn't contain now: targets and UHC visit counts switch to the new month hours early. Checked with bikram-sambat 1.8.0 under TZ=Asia/Kathmandu: 2024-05-13 19:00 (Baisakh 31) gives 2024-05-14..2024-06-14. The tests use local-midnight dates, and the 'Timezone boundaries' test's 15:00Z reads as Baisakh 9 instead of 8, which stays inside the same month, so it passes by chance. Fix: toBik(referenceDate.format('YYYY-MM-DD')).
required.match: Says toBik is given a Date/timestamp rather than a date string (or that the BS conversion depends on the time of day or timezone), so the reference date can be converted to the wrong BS day and the wrong interval returned. A general comment that the tests don't cover timezones, without saying the conversion is wrong, is not a match.

required.summary: getTargetIntervalTag finds the PREVIOUS period by subtracting monthsAgo Gregorian months from the current interval's end. BS intervals run from mid-month to mid-month (Baisakh 2081 is 2024-04-13..2024-05-13), so end minus one month (2024-04-13) usually falls inside the current interval and the 'previous' tag equals the current one: 9 of 12 months in 2024-25 with month_start_date 1. The supervisor 'last month' target aggregates then show the current month, and fetchTargetDocs (target-aggregates.service.ts:53, monthsOld 0..N) fetches the same month repeatedly and skips older ones. Stepping back from interval.start minus one day, as #11237 does, avoids it.
required.match: Says that with BS intervals, subtracting a (Gregorian) month from the current interval's end can land in the current interval, so the previous-period tag/interval is the current one (or otherwise wrong). Only saying the month label shown is Gregorian is not a match: that is reporting-month-gregorian-name.

required.summary: SearchService.getLastVisitedDates, which computes the contacts list's UHC visit counts and last-visited sort, still calls CalendarInterval.getCurrent(settings.monthStartDate) without the BS flag, though the visitCountSettings it receives from contacts.component now carry useBikramSambatMonths. With the flag on, the contacts list counts visits per Gregorian interval while the contact summary (uhc-stats.service) counts per BS month, so the two disagree.
required.match: Names search.service / getLastVisitedDates (or the contacts list visit counts) as still using Gregorian intervals because the BS flag isn't passed.

required.summary: When month_start_date is larger than the previous BS month's length (30 or 31 against a 29/30-day month), the else branch clamps the interval start to that month's last day, while the preceding interval's end is clamped to the same day (intervalStartDate - 1 capped at daysInCurrent). That day belongs to two intervals. E.g. month_start_date 31: 2024-02-12..2024-03-13 and 2024-03-13..2024-04-12 both contain 2024-03-13 (Falgun 30), so visits and target emissions on it count in both months. The Gregorian code instead starts the interval on the 1st of the following month. The PR's 'clamps intervalStartDate' test asserts the overlapping start.
required.match: Says that for a start day past the end of a short BS month, consecutive intervals overlap (or share a day), or that the clamping differs from the Gregorian rule in a way that double-counts a day. Only saying normalizeStartDate can't express day 32 is not a match. Only saying the clamp differs from the Gregorian rule, without saying that a day falls in two intervals or is counted twice, is not a match.

required.summary: The PR updates no existing spec, and several now fail. rules-engine.service.spec.ts mocks UHCSettingsService as { getMonthStartDate } only, so getRulesSettings, fetchTargets and getTargetIntervalTag throw calling shouldEnableBikramSambatMonths. getVisitCountSettings now always adds useBikramSambatMonths (false when off), breaking the deep.equal assertions in uhc-settings.service.spec.ts and contacts.component.spec.ts. The rules state now always carries useBikramSambatMonths (undefined when unset), breaking provider-wireup.spec.js's deep.eq on the stored state; #11237 had to add the key to those expectations.
required.match: Says an existing spec will fail because of this change: the UHCSettingsService mock lacking shouldEnableBikramSambatMonths, the extra useBikramSambatMonths key breaking deep-equal assertions, or similar. Only saying the webapp or rules-engine changes have no new tests is not a match: that is no-integration-tests.

extra_credit.summary: getMonthStartDate's `||` became `??`, so a falsy but non-null uhc.month_start_date (0, '' or false) no longer falls back to uhc.visit_count.month_start_date; it is returned, and normalizeStartDate turns it into 1. A behaviour change for existing Gregorian configs that the PR, which says Gregorian behaviour is unchanged, doesn't mention.
extra_credit.match: Says replacing `||` with `??` changes the fallback for falsy month_start_date values.

extra_credit.summary: getReportingMonth formats the Gregorian YYYY-MM tag as a month name, so with BS months on, the targets UI labels Baisakh (ending 2024-05-13) as 'May'. The tag format is the #10652 design, but the label shown to users is misleading; #11237 maps it to BS month names.
extra_credit.match: Says the month name shown for target aggregates/reporting period is the Gregorian month, not the BS month.

extra_credit.summary: getCurrent and getPrevious overload their second parameter as either a reference date or the BS flag, chosen by typeof === 'boolean'. Callers like rules-state-store and the webapp CalendarIntervalService pass the flag positionally, so a non-boolean truthy flag (e.g. a string from config) would be taken as a reference date. An options object or a separate parameter order would be clearer.
extra_credit.match: Says the boolean/date overload of the second parameter is fragile or confusing.

extra_credit.summary: fetchTargets now awaits settingsService.get() on every call to read the BS flag, while uhcMonthStartDate is cached once in assignMonthStartDate. The flag could be cached alongside it.
extra_credit.match: Says fetchTargets re-reads settings on each call, or that the BS flag should be cached like uhcMonthStartDate.

extra_credit.summary: Only the calendar-interval library is tested. Nothing tests the rules-state-store, rules-engine.service, uhc-settings or uhc-stats changes, which is where previous-tag-is-current and last-visited-still-gregorian sit.
extra_credit.match: Says the webapp services or rules-engine changes have no tests. Saying existing specs now fail is existing-specs-break.

rejected.summary: Target docs (provider-wireup storeTargetsDoc) and the DHIS export (api/src/services/export/dhis.js) still use Gregorian YYYY-MM tags, so BS-month target docs collide or can't be found.
rejected.reason: Keeping the Gregorian YYYY-MM of the interval end is the design agreed in #10652 and the PR says it keeps the storage format. A BS month never starts and ends in the same Gregorian month, so each BS interval's end falls in a distinct Gregorian month: tags stay unique, and the writer (provider-wireup) and the CURRENT-period reader (getTargetIntervalTag) agree. The real tag bug is the PREVIOUS-period lookup (previous-tag-is-current).
rejected.match: Says target doc ids/tags, provider-wireup or the DHIS export must switch to BS year-month or else docs collide or go missing. Pointing out the PREVIOUS-period lookup returns the current tag is previous-tag-is-current, not this.

rejected.summary: bikram-sambat is a new dependency of @medic/calendar-interval with no lockfile entry, so it won't be installed or resolvable.
rejected.reason: cht-core's root package.json and package-lock.json already depend on bikram-sambat ^1.8.0 (the webapp uses it for date formatting), and calendar-interval has no lockfile of its own, so it resolves.
rejected.match: Says bikram-sambat is missing, unresolvable or needs a lockfile/install step.

requirements.notes: There is no linked issue, so requirements come from the PR description only; a report that says so is right. Reports split and merge requirements differently, so each item is matched by meaning, and one report item may cover several. `status` is the bucket it should land in; `acceptable` lists other buckets that are not counted as a miss. Report items for trivial PR bullets match nothing and are not scored. `preconditions_to_confirm` holds the operational facts the skill should list under 'Preconditions to confirm'. `rejected` holds findings reviews are likely to make that are wrong.
